summary:
Snapshot from 5 Nov 2026. The top opportunities this week are practical tirzepatide questions where we can get in early. Five items from the playbook's Lane A long-form queue are still open: injection site reactions, fatigue, birth control (label only), dehydration and an aftercare/after-stopping refresh. The Thanksgiving Shorts funnel is the strongest seasonal play, with the Nov 18–27 peak 2–3 weeks away (momentum 78 to 84 over 10 snapshots).

Three new emerging hooks are worth a Short now:
- Nail changes: the EADV 2026 survey reported nail detachment in 39% of users vs 9% of non-users. Dermatology Digest picked it up again on Nov 4, and few creators have covered it.
- Holiday drinking: a new semaglutide/tirzepatide alcohol-outcomes study (Diabetes Obes Metab, Nov 3) plus EMJ's alcohol-cravings story (Nov 4).
- Menopause hormone therapy: an observational study linked it to bigger weight loss on tirzepatide (19.2% vs 14%), back in the news via Newsweek on Nov 3.

Watch ObesityWeek (Nov 14–17) for the full REDEFINE 4 results (CagriSema vs tirzepatide). That's the only likely trigger for a head-to-head extra long-form.

Prediabetes vs metformin (AHA) is peaking. Wegovy pill earnings coverage is business news. Only use them with a differentiated angle.

Reject:
- online programs, sellers and price stories
- the compounded tirzepatide recall and Empower lawsuit
- retatrutide 'supplier' listicles
- 'natural GLP-1 alternative' supplement roundups

Verification notes:
- The ABC heat-wave GLP-1 story is a July 2026 piece resurfacing, so only use it as a hook for Australia's summer.
- Stanford's 'natural Ozempic' (BRP) is a 2025 animal study in Nature being recirculated.
- The search couldn't independently confirm the TGA approval of the Wegovy pill (The Guardian and Australian Pharmacist report it). The fact-checker must confirm it on the TGA site.
- Washington poison-centre calls are mostly about dosing confusion with compounded vials.

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: getting full fast, eating slower at the table, protein first, alcohol and easing nausea at a big holiday meal (Shorts funnel to the live Thanksgiving long-form)
candidates.angle: Calm 'Will I be able to enjoy Thanksgiving on tirzepatide?' Shorts. The hook is the Sun Sentinel advice column (Nov 4) where a reader says GLP-1 friends 'eat so fast' at dinner. We turn it around: slowing down, a small plate and protein first help with fullness and nausea. Each Short ends by pointing to the Thanksgiving long-form. No weight talk, just enjoying the meal.
candidates.why_now: It has grown steadily across 10 snapshots (78 to 84). Food press (FoodNavigator: 'GLP-1 users redefining indulgence'; Sun Sentinel advice column) is building toward the holiday. Search demand peaks the week of Thanksgiving, and Shorts posted 2–3 weeks early have time to rank and send viewers to the long-form.

evidence.signal: Mainstream advice column on GLP-1 users eating fast at shared dinners: a social-eating question people are asking
Food industry coverage of how GLP-1 users approach indulgent foods

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: what's normal (redness, itching, small lumps), what the label reports, and when to call your prescriber
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Tirzepatide Injection Site Reactions: Normal?' The first sentence answers the question (most reported reactions are mild and short-lived; give the label's rates vs placebo). Then a 'you just noticed a red spot' scenario, and chapters named after the searches people make (itching, lumps, bruising, rotating sites as the label's instructions describe, signs to call your prescriber). Use a state-change thumbnail (worried → answered). No dosing.
keywords: is redness normal after tirzepatide shot
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; steady search demand, best shipped within 7 days
candidates.why_now: Momentum rose from 72 to 80 over 8 snapshots. Its Short reached 223 views by day 2, our fastest start since the hair Short. It's next in the playbook's Lane A queue and sits right next to the Side Effects video (480 min, carried by suggested video).

evidence.signal: Injection-site Short: 223 views by day 2; listed as a priority Lane A long-form
GLP-1 exposure calls rising, many from injection/dosing confusion with vials, which reinforces the need for clear, label-based injection education

candidates.topic: Why am I so tired on tirzepatide? Label fatigue rates (5%, 6%, 7% across doses vs 3% on placebo) and the everyday drivers (eating much less, too little fluid, nausea, sleep)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Tirzepatide Fatigue: Why Am I So Tired?' Answer first (fatigue is listed more often than on placebo, and for most people it's manageable). Then the 'it's 3 pm and you're wiped out' scenario. Cover protein, fluids, sleep and gentle movement, plus when tiredness is a reason to call your prescriber. Absolute rates only, no dosing.
keywords: why am i so tired on mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Seen in 5 snapshots at a steady 80–82. Yahoo's 'GLP-1s and fatigue' piece (Oct 30) kept the question in mainstream feeds. It's a Lane A queue item, and it links naturally to What to Eat and Protein.

evidence.signal: Label lists fatigue more often with tirzepatide than with placebo
Health-system explainer on GLP-1s; patient questions about side effects remain high

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and nail changes: is nail lifting or discoloration normal? EADV 2026 survey: nail detachment in 39% of GLP-1 users vs 9% of metabolically similar non-users
candidates.angle: Body-worry Short: 'Tirzepatide and Your Nails: Is This Normal?' It's a self-reported survey covering the GLP-1 class, and about half the users had nail problems before starting. Researchers think fast weight loss and lower food intake may be behind it, not the drug directly. Give the honest answer: 'linked to', not 'causes'. Add a protein and nutrition tip, and say when to see a doctor or dermatologist (pain, infection signs). It could pair with the hair-loss long-form as the 'watch next'.
candidates.why_now: The EADV congress study (Oct 2026) spread through medical outlets (HCPLive, Medical Economics, Becker's, MDLinx), and Dermatology Digest revisited it on Nov 4. Consumer creators have barely covered it yet. It follows the same body-worry pattern as our best Short (hair grow-back, 1,015 views).

evidence.signal: 'GLP-1 RA Use and Nail Detachment: What's the Connection?'
Nail detachment 4× more common with GLP-1 use (EADV 2026)
Multinational study: 39% vs 9% nail detachment; caveats on pre-existing problems

candidates.topic: Does tirzepatide change how alcohol feels at holiday parties? New target-trial emulation of semaglutide and tirzepatide and alcohol-related outcomes in type 2 diabetes (Diabetes Obes Metab, Nov 3) plus the EMJ 'GLP-1s cut alcohol cravings' report (Nov 4)
candidates.angle: Short: 'Tirzepatide and Alcohol: Why One Drink Feels Different'. Cover what's confirmed: observational studies link these medicines to fewer alcohol-related hospital visits, and trials are still under way. For the holidays: a drink on an emptier stomach, dehydration and nausea. We don't encourage or discourage drinking. Say to ask your prescriber about alcohol. It could become a seasonal Lane A long-form later ('Tirzepatide and Alcohol: What to Know').
candidates.why_now: Fresh study on Nov 3 plus EMJ news on Nov 4, and earlier snapshots picked up the Heineken 'GLP-1 problem' and a PET-imaging trial protocol. Thanksgiving through New Year is when people search 'can I drink on…'.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide, Tirzepatide and Clinically Recorded Alcohol-Related Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Target Trial Emulation
'GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Cut Alcohol Cravings'
Newer GLP-1 RA initiation linked to 22–32% lower risk of alcohol-related hospitalization in adults with AUD (observational)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and birth control pills: what the label says about reduced oral contraceptive exposure, plus the pregnancy-outcomes meta-analysis (Front Pharmacol, Oct 16)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Tirzepatide and Birth Control: What to Know'. Report what the label says, word for word: why oral contraceptives may work less well, and the timing the label describes around starting and dose increases. No instructions. Send viewers to their prescriber, plus a pregnancy-planning section. Calm and practical.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 9 snapshots across three phrasings. It's in the Lane A queue, and few creators cover it from the label. New pregnancy-outcome literature (Oct 2026) makes it current.

evidence.signal: Time-window-stratified meta-analysis of pregnancy outcomes after GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP exposure
Label section on oral hormonal contraceptives

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and dehydration: signs and what helps (the label's acute kidney injury warning linked to vomiting and diarrhoea), hooked to Australian summer heat
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Tirzepatide and Dehydration: Signs and What Helps'. Explain why appetite and thirst cues can both drop, the signs (dark urine, dizziness, headache, fatigue), and fluid habits for hot days and sick days. Explain the label's kidney warning calmly and say when to call your prescriber. The ABC/GMA heat story is from July, so present it as a seasonal reminder, not news.
candidates.why_now: The ABC/GMA heat-wave story resurfaced in feeds again (Nov 4). Australia is going into summer, and AU is a high-CPM audience. It's in the Lane A queue and connects to the fatigue and constipation videos.

evidence.source: ABC News / Good Morning America (resurfaced Nov 4; first published July 2026)
evidence.signal: Doctors warn GLP-1 users about dehydration risks in heat
Local outlets repeat doctor warnings on GLP-1 dehydration

candidates.topic: Life after stopping tirzepatide: why 'aftercare' matters. EMJ expert warning (Nov 4) on neglected GLP-1 aftercare despite regain risk, plus adherence and persistence coverage (Amgen, AJMC)
candidates.angle: Funnel Short (20:00) that sends viewers to the live stopping long-form: 'Tirzepatide: Will Hunger Come Back If You Stop?' Use SURMOUNT-4 and its exact population. Explain that plans for keeping results (protein, strength, follow-up) are something to work out with your prescriber. Include 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'.
keywords: what happens when you stop mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Three independent pieces on persistence and aftercare came out Nov 3–4 (EMJ, Amgen, AJMC). The redone stopping long-form shipped on 11-04 and needs Shorts pointing to it. January resolution searches are 8 weeks away.

evidence.signal: 'GLP-1 Aftercare Neglected Despite Weight Regain Risk, Expert Warns'
Early treatment trajectory and long-term persistence to semaglutide for obesity
'Why GLP-1 adherence, not access, decides value'

candidates.topic: Menopause hormone therapy and tirzepatide: observational study of about 3,900 women aged 45+ linked HT use to greater weight loss (19.2% vs 14% on tirzepatide; about 11% vs 9.5% on semaglutide at 1 year)
candidates.angle: Short: 'Tirzepatide After Menopause: Does Hormone Therapy Matter?' It's observational, so 'linked to', not 'causes'. Women on HT may differ in other ways, and there's no randomized trial yet. Mention the estrogen–GLP-1 animal research as a possible reason. This is not a reason to start HT. Say to talk to your doctor about menopause care. It fits the large 45–65 female audience.
candidates.why_now: Newsweek (Nov 3) revived the study after Fox, MedicineNet and health-library syndication in October. Menopause plus GLP-1 is a high-interest crossover topic with thin YouTube coverage from the evidence angle.

evidence.signal: 'Hormone Therapy Linked to How Some Women Respond to GLP-1 Weight Loss Drugs'
Study details: ~3,900 women, 19.2% vs 14% with tirzepatide

candidates.topic: ObesityWeek 2026 (Nov 14–17): full REDEFINE 4 results, CagriSema vs tirzepatide in adults with obesity (open-label, 84 weeks; topline about 23% with CagriSema, non-inferiority to tirzepatide not met), plus possible retatrutide data
candidates.angle: Get ready now and publish within 48 h of the presentation. A 13:00 Short with tirzepatide named first: 'Tirzepatide vs CagriSema: The Full Results'. It's the only kind of news that qualifies for an extra L2 long-form (a randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide, made public within the last 48 h). Novo says it's eyeing a US launch of CagriSema, which raises interest.
candidates.why_now: Novo's Q3 call (Nov 4) highlighted the CagriSema US launch plans, and BioSpace is covering the Lilly vs Novo data fight. Full head-to-head data at ObesityWeek is a scheduled spike, and the analysis gets very little coverage outside pharma trade press.

evidence.signal: Novo eyes US launch of CagriSema
Novo and Lilly trade data blows in the oral GLP-1 race

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines vs metformin in prediabetes with obesity (AHA Scientific Sessions 2026): observational EHR study of 256,492 adults linked to 31% lower type 2 diabetes risk and 1.5× the chance of blood sugar returning to normal
candidates.angle: Different angle for a topic that's peaking: 'Prediabetes and Tirzepatide: Who It's Actually Approved For'. The study is observational and not yet peer-reviewed. Explain that GLP-1 medicines aren't approved for prediabetes alone, that weight-management approval criteria are based on BMI plus weight-related conditions, and give viewers questions to bring to their doctor. Add natural GLP-1 support habits (protein, fibre, movement) without claiming they replace the medicine.
candidates.why_now: Reuters, US News, HealthDay, heart.org and international outlets all ran it on Nov 2–4. Coverage is near saturation, so it's only worth doing with the 'who it's approved for' angle.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 meds linked to lower diabetes and heart risks than metformin
'GLP-1 Drugs Can Help Reverse Prediabetes, Researchers Report'

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and your bones: new systematic review and meta-analysis of GLP-1 RAs and bone metabolism in placebo-controlled RCTs (Bone, Nov 2; mostly first-generation agents)
candidates.angle: Body-worry Short: 'Tirzepatide and Bones: Will They Weaken?' Report what RCTs of the class show, and say that most of the trials used older GLP-1 drugs, so it's not tirzepatide-specific. Strength training and protein are protective habits. Send viewers to the Bones & Muscle long-form (80% AVD). Use 'GLP-1 medicines' for class-level findings.
candidates.why_now: A fresh RCT meta-analysis (Nov 2) plus a corrected pilot trial in older adults (Front Aging). Our bones Short reached 242 views, and the Bones & Muscle long-form needs funnel traffic.

evidence.signal: Systematic review and meta-analysis of GLP-1 RAs on bone metabolism (placebo-controlled RCTs, predominantly first-generation)
BMD and turnover response to GLP-1 RAs in older adults, 20-week pilot post hoc (correction)

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines after 65 and frailty: JAMA analysis (Oct 30) of SELECT's semaglutide heart results across frailty levels
candidates.angle: Short: 'Tirzepatide and GLP-1s After 65: Safe If You're Frail?' Report the semaglutide SELECT frailty findings in their exact population (heart disease plus overweight/obesity, no diabetes), then why protein and strength matter more with age. Questions to ask your doctor. Semaglutide named for the SELECT data only.
candidates.why_now: JAMA (Oct 30) plus a Front Pharmacol analysis of age-stratified evidence (Oct 20), and Skilled Nursing News on GLP-1s reaching nursing homes (Nov 2). Older adults are a large, high-CPM part of the audience, and few creators cover them well.

evidence.signal: 'Are GLP-1 Drugs Safe in People With Frailty?'
Availability of age-stratified evidence for GLP-1 RAs in EU assessment reports

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill reported approved in Australia (TGA, per The Guardian and Australian Pharmacist, Nov 3–4): how a daily tablet differs from weekly tirzepatide and semaglutide injections
candidates.angle: 13:00 Short for the AU audience: 'Tirzepatide Shot vs the New Semaglutide Pill'. Cover the practical differences (daily tablet with fasting rules from the label vs weekly injection), and say it's separate trials, not head-to-head. No price or access talk. Brand names for recognition only. The fact-checker must confirm the TGA approval on the TGA site first, because our search couldn't confirm it independently.
candidates.why_now: The Guardian AU and The Conversation explainers (Nov 4) plus heavy Novo Q3 coverage of the pill's rollout to 8 markets. AU viewers are searching for 'how does it differ'.

evidence.signal: 'Australia's first GLP-1 weight-loss pill has been approved. How does it differ to injections?'
'New GLP-1 RA weight-loss tablet approved in Australia'

candidates.topic: Retatrutide 'what's confirmed': not approved, online 'research' products aren't the trial drug. Forbes on online-sales risks (Nov 4), Malaysia's Health Ministry seizes RM341,000 of unapproved retatrutide (Nov 2), and US compounding-oversight bill advancing amid FDA warnings
candidates.angle: Use the one gray-market Short allowed this week: 'Retatrutide: What's Confirmed So Far'. Phase 3 results are real (cite them by name and population), but it isn't approved anywhere. Products sold online aren't the trial drug, and regulators are seizing them. Loop ending. Name no sellers and give no access routes.
candidates.why_now: Several independent signals on Nov 2–4 (Forbes, Malaysian seizures, GaBI on the FDA and compounding bill, Town & Country 'Ret Is the Word'). Search for retatrutide is high, and our retatrutide 'what's confirmed' Shorts have done well (209–278).

evidence.signal: 'Retatrutide: What To Know About Online Sales, Safety Risks and More'
Health Ministry seizes RM341,000 of unapproved retatrutide

candidates.topic: Stanford's 'natural Ozempic' BRP peptide (ScienceDaily Nov 4): AI-discovered 12-amino-acid peptide that cut food intake in mice and minipigs (Nature, 2025), no human trials yet
candidates.angle: Only as a myth-check Short: 'Is There a Natural Tirzepatide?' Cover what's confirmed: animal studies only, no human data, and nothing you can buy. Bridge to the body's own GLP-1 and evidence-based habits (protein, fibre, eating order) without claiming they replace the medicine. Don't call it new; the study is from 2025.
candidates.why_now: ScienceDaily repost (Nov 4) of the 2025 Nature study. 'Natural Ozempic' is a magnet for supplement misinformation, so a myth-check fills a gap. But there's no new science, and it attracts low-quality supplement content.

evidence.signal: 'AI helps Stanford scientists discover a natural Ozempic'; preclinical, Nature 2025

candidates.topic: GLP-1 poison-centre calls doubling in Washington: mostly dosing mix-ups, about half linked to compounded vials
candidates.angle: If it's used at all, a calm 'use your pen exactly as your prescriber and pharmacist showed you, and call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 if a mistake happens' line inside an injection long-form. No dose numbers, no vial or syringe instructions, and no Short of its own.
candidates.why_now: KIRO 7 (Nov 4) is a local story. A standalone video would edge toward dosing and compounded content, which our guardrails ban.

evidence.signal: 'GLP-1 poison calls double in Washington'
About half of calls involve compounded semaglutide/tirzepatide vials; 10-fold overdoses reported

candidates.topic: Bariatric surgery after GLP-1 intolerance or limited weight loss (Cleveland Clinic / Ann Surg, Nov 3)
candidates.angle: Not a priority. Surgery angles underperform (8–15 views) and it's a single observational study. At most, mention in passing that other options exist, in a long-form on what to discuss with your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: A fresh study plus a Cleveland Clinic press release, but our analytics show surgery angles don't perform for this audience.

evidence.signal: Bariatric Surgery as a Rescue Strategy After Semaglutide or Tirzepatide
